Digitized and made available on the BCHC website the
"Purchase of Land for Camp Hood - Landowners." The
history of present-day Fort Hood dates back to 1942 and the
formation of Camp Hood, a training area for World War II
troops. A binder in the archives of the Bell County Historical
Commission includes information about the landowners
involved in the government's acquisition of land required to
create and expand Camp Hood. Organized alphabetically by
landowner name, the information appears to have been
abstracted from documentation associated with the land
transactions and includes details such as the acreage, price
per acre, and pertinent dates for each transaction.

The Maxdale Bridge, a RTHL in Bell County, has been
unused and is abandoned and has been a victim of
vandalism and defacing of the grounds, embankments, and
approaches. The THC historical marker was removed by
vandals and discarded on the property and is kept in the
BCHC for safekeeping. After discussion at a meeting about
moving the bridge, the BCHC coordinated withe the County
Division of Architecture in their efforts to prevent
pedestrians from accessing the bridge. The County
prepared a a written plan for the safety enhancements on
the bridge ends to remove the earth embankment on the
approaches, and then add signs and fence it to prevent
trespassing.

On Sunday, May 26, 1839, Republic of Texas Captain John
Bird and his party of 35 Texas Rangers set out to chase
three native Americans from the Little River fort built under
the supervision of Sgt. George B. Erath (1836) in what is
now Bell County. After a running battle that carried the
Rangers over 11 miles into the Cherokee Nation, the
Rangers faced upwards of 200 natives and retreated to a
ravine alongside what is now named Bird's Creek. After
seven hours and multiple waves of attacks the Rangers
prevailed and escaped into the darkness, however Bird and
four other men died as a result of the battle. In 2022 the
land was bought and is under development for a sub-
division when Bell County resident Chaz Parker notified the
THC of his concern of a 1936 Centennial historical marker
was in disrepair near the site of the battle. The BCHC, in
partnership with the City of Temple, the Texas Historical
Commission, the Texas Ranger Hall of Fame, the property
owners WB Development, and the Land Acquisition
managers DR Horton have entered a collaborative
agreement to relocate the historic marker closer to the
ravine and to create a preservation and interpretation
initiative to tell the story of the battle from both sides of the
conflict. The City of Temple has sponsored a request to
relocate the historic marker and is creating interpretive
signage. WB Development and DR Horton have redesigned
the plans to section off the battlefield site and to create a
park-like setting with sidewalks and benches to view the
battlefield. The project is ongoing and may take 18-24
months to complete.

Q34
Project Description #1 –– Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
On April 14th officers of the Bell County Historical Commission participated in an open-house community meeting in the City of Temple
about historic preservation. Coordinated by the Temple Senior Planner and Historic Preservation Officer Kelly Atkinson, the meeting
was held from 5:30-7:00 PM at the historic Santa Fe Train Depot. The Commission set-up an information booth and offered information
and a specially designed flyer about BCHC to general public guests and history-minded organizations who browsed from table to table
to learn about local historic preservation activities and organizations. This was the City's first event of this type in recent memory and
the Commission looks forward to support future events.

Q35
Project Description #2 –– Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
The Bell County Historical Commission awarded four grants in 2022 totaling $7865. Each year, the commission accepts grant
applications September 1 through October 31 and considers any project, except construction, for funding. Non-profit, tax-exempt
organizations or institutions located in Bell County are eligible to apply. Grants approved in 2022 for disbursement in 2023 were:
1. Carpenter Cemetery - $865.00: Purchase of stone bases for headstones on the graves of Marshall Crawford (1879) and T.B.
Crawford (1860).
2. Bartlett Activity Center - $4,500.00: Renovation of the building’s historic bell tower. This old red brick activity center, originally the
1909 grammar school, is the only remaining building by Austin architect A.O. Watson.
3. Dyess Family Cemetery - $ 1,500.00: Conduct of a 2023 boundary and border establishment project at this historic East Bell County
cemetery that contains graves of some of the early settlers. The land around the cemetery is being clear cut for a solar farm. Having
a legal survey performed was recommended by the Texas Historical Commission in 2021, when the cemetery was granted historical
status. The Dyess Family Cemetery Association will match $1,500.00 to complete this project.
4. Salado Historical Society - $1,000.00: A portion of the cost for the walkway path to two historic log cabins, including the Denman
Cabin The M. H. Denman Cabin is a Recorded Texas Historical Landmark and was presented a historical marker in 1968. The
inscription reads "M.H. Denman built cabin 1867 (15 mi. NW), of handhewn, square cedar logs joined by wooden pegs; has fireplace of
native stone; restored 1955. Recorded Texas Historic Landmark.

Q36
Project Description #3 –– Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
Historic document donations to southwest collection at Texas Tech University On Monday September 26, 2022 the BCHC donated
historical documents to the Southwest Collection at Texas Tech University. Work involved collecting, organizing, and multiple archival
boxes of historically significant items for donation. The items include documents, photographs, post cards, letters, ledgers, and
brochures associated with Texas and Bell County that were part of two personal archives, the Kelsey Collection and the Handler
Collection; and information gathered through personal interviews and research of various sources concerning the wartime experiences
of military veterans and civilians during World War II. Placement of the items with the Southwest Collection helps to ensure availability
of the information for future generations.

Q37
Share your thoughts on THC and/or CHC Outreach services that have helped your CHC.
During a discussion of the Nominating Committee for officers of the 2023-2024 years, the Nomionating Committee Chair was faced
with a discrepancy in understanding rules in regard to the Texas Code as it relates to County Historical Commissions. The Chair called
the THC office that works with CHCs and discussed the issue with a staffer. The response was well thought out and informative, and
helped the Chair resolve the issue and to be able to press on and complete the nomination cycle. The support provided to Bell County
by the THC office was notable, and appreciated, by the Chair, and worthy of recognition.
